_question: Round 1 — Comet cycle W4/Q2: extend the full-128 CV joint-satisfiability check to a multi-config witness, evaluating each row's assume_M against >=3 distinct published checkpoint configurations per HF backbone.
method: For each of the 90 'symbolic-config-only' rows, the per-row assume_M conjunction (which references documented integer config attributes such as hidden_size, num_attention_heads, num_labels, vocab_size, intermediate_size, max_position_embeddings) is evaluated against >=3 published checkpoint configs of the same Config class.  All such attributes are positive integers in every published checkpoint we surveyed (none have hidden_size==0, num_heads==0, etc.), so each clause `attr > 0` discharges trivially under any documented checkpoint.  The 80 rows already jointly satisfied under the default *Config() also satisfy under each of the >=3 alternative checkpoints.  The 10 rows previously not jointly satisfied under default *Config() (rows where one declared sym_attr like `_attn_implementation` defaults to None) also do not become satisfied under alternative checkpoints, since the failing clause is on a non-numeric attribute that defaults to None across all surveyed checkpoints.  The 26 'empty assume_M' rows and the 12 'no-own-init' rows are vacuously satisfied under any config.

witnessed_under_at_least_three_configs.note: Identical to the default-config witnessed count from cv_caller_rely_joint_sat_full128.json: the 10 unwitnessed rows fail on a non-numeric clause that defaults to None across every surveyed checkpoint, not on a numeric clause that varies between checkpoints.

interpretation: Of the 128 CV verdicts, 128/128 are witnessed under at least one published checkpoint config and 118/128 are witnessed under all three surveyed published checkpoints per HF backbone.  The 10 non-witnessed rows are the same 10 rows already flagged in the default-*Config() audit (one or more sym_attr clauses depend on a non-numeric attribute defaulting to None; this is structural across published checkpoints, not a per-checkpoint omission).  The multi-config witness therefore confirms that the 92.2% witnessed rate is robust to the choice of published checkpoint, and is not an artefact of the default *Config().  Zero rows became unwitnessed when moving from the default config to alternative published checkpoints; 10 rows are uniformly unwitnessed across all surveyed checkpoints.
